Forecasting Inflation Using News Feeds: BERTopic vs. LDA ... Forecasting inflation is an important applied problem. One way to improve inflation forecasting is to extract features from news, since, firstly, news may contain information about important events that directly or indirectly affect inflation, and secondly, news may affect inflation expectations. One of the most popular methods of extracting features from text in economic literature is topic modeling. This paper is devoted to a comparative analysis of two topic extraction methods - BERTopic, which is based on neural networks and used for the first time in this paper, and the more popular LDA, which is based on the analysis of the frequency distribution of words in texts - for forecasting inflation in Russia using data from popular Telegram channels.

Think about it this way, each paper in an ACL conference year is reduced to a single number: the median reference age. So if in 2021, you cite only BERT* papers, your median reference age will be about 2 or 3. But if you cite Penn Treebank style papers, your median reference age will be much higher.

We joke about how nobody cites papers older than 5 years any more, but every generation believes that “back in my day, things were better”. How true is it actually? This is an empirical question, and thanks to the amazing ACL Anthology, we can answer it. To do this, I used the Semantic Scholar API to gather the title, authors, and references for most ACL papers going back to the beginning (1979).

This brings the average reference age down, even if all references to relevant “old” papers remain. But looking from 2005 to 2014 or so, reference age increased even as publication and reference list sizes increased. This suggests that in those years, authors tended to not cite recent work, which may be a sign of stagnation.
